jobs.title: Data analyst (H/F)
jobs.description:
Role Overview
The Data Analyst (H/F) is responsible for transforming complex datasets into clear, actionable insights that support strategic planning and operational improvement. This role involves gathering data from various sources, performing detailed analyses, and presenting findings to stakeholders across the organization. The Data Analyst ensures data accuracy, builds reporting tools, and contributes to the development of data-driven solutions. This position is ideal for analytical professionals who enjoy problem-solving, critical thinking, and working with diverse teams.
Key Responsibilities
• Collect, clean, and organize data from multiple systems and databases to ensure high-quality datasets.
• Perform exploratory and advanced analyses to identify trends, opportunities, and areas for optimization.
• Design and maintain dashboards, automated reports, and visualization tools for internal teams.
• Collaborate with departments such as marketing, operations, finance, and product to understand analytical needs.
• Support performance tracking by monitoring KPIs and providing regular updates.
• Translate complex analytical results into clear, understandable insights for decision-makers.
• Assist in the development of forecasting models and analytical methodologies.
• Document data processes, standards, and definitions to strengthen data governance.
• Conduct quality checks on datasets and recommend improvements for data integrity.
• Stay informed about emerging tools, techniques, and best practices in analytics.
Qualifications and Requirements
• Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Economics, or a related discipline.
• 1–3 years of experience in data analysis, business intelligence, or a similar analytical role.
• Proficiency with analytical tools such as SQL, Excel, Python, or R.
• Experience working with visualization platforms such as Tableau, Power BI, or equivalent tools.
• Strong understanding of analytical methods, statistical concepts, and data modeling.
• High attention to detail with strong organizational and problem-solving skills.
• Ability to communicate analytical findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
• Comfortable managing multiple tasks and deadlines in a dynamic environment.
• Strong collaboration and interpersonal skills for cross-functional teamwork.
• Proactive mindset with a desire to learn, improve processes, and contribute to data-driven culture.
Summary
The Data Analyst (H/F) plays a vital role in enabling informed decision-making across the organization. By analyzing data, developing meaningful insights, and collaborating with key stakeholders, this role supports growth, efficiency, and strategic direction. It is well-suited for analytical and detail-oriented professionals committed to delivering accurate and impactful insights.

jobs.description:
Summary

Job Summary

The CU Student Government Program Coordinator plays a crucial role in supporting CU Student Government (CUSG) across its various branches, including the Executive Branch, Legislative Branch, Judicial Branch, Election Commission, Joint Boards, and Finance Board. This position is responsible for supporting CU Student Government in various administrative functions, including student leader support, hiring, onboarding and managing student employees and leaders, fiscal review and planning, procurement and CUSG board relations.

CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment. We are committed to creating a workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities.

Who We Are

The Division of Student Life consists of 36 departments that provide student support and services dedicated to helping students become successful, curious, competent individuals during their time at CU Boulder.

CU Student Government (CUSG)

The University of Colorado Student Government (CUSG) is the official governing body of the over 38,000 students at CU Boulder. As the most autonomous student government in the nation, CUSG is responsible for allocating $37 million in student fees to improve the lives of all CU Boulder students. CUSG seeks to make a meaningful impact on the lives of CU Boulder students through advocacy, representation, allocation and legislation.

Responsibilities

What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be

Student Leader Support

Post and track student job and leadership opportunity announcements using Handshake and other CU specified avenues.
Receive, organize, and forward incoming applications to the appropriate hiring committee.
Inform and provide resources to each member of a hiring committee of CU Boulder’s policy on hiring student employees and best practices while conducting an interview.
Develop and implement position-specific hiring timelines for all CUSG’s positions and student leader positions to ensure compliance with university policy.
Assist in the design and facilitation of training and development for CUSG positions, student staff, and student leader positions.
Schedule interviews with CUSG branch leaders and appropriate stakeholders.
Coordinate the submission and approval of student employee timesheets, handling hiring and onboarding processes, exit procedures, and leave reconciliation.
Supervise and manage departmental student employees.

Administrative Support

Serve as the CUSG liaison with Student Life Employee Experience Liaison, to ensure payroll is processed for part-time salaried and student employees.
Work directly with Student Life Employee Experience to hire all student employees and leaders for CUSG, ensuring accurate pay amounts and term dates.
Assist employees with timekeeping submissions, ensuring accurate and timely processing of bi-weekly and monthly payroll.
Review and monitor CUSG’s student budget with a focus on ensuring staff stays within approved hours and aligns with CU Boulder policy.
In collaboration with Student Life Employee Experience, troubleshoot payroll issues related to hiring, onboarding, and exit procedures.
Coordinate onboarding instructions and support for new student staff hires around payroll information, hiring packets, work-study, supervisory change forms, and separating student staff leaving their position.
Coordinate with Student Life Employee Experience on payroll-related inquiries, hiring transactions, and payment discrepancies.
Manage users and permissions within relevant software, managing accounts and permissions as necessary.
Assist other users in troubleshooting issues related to software used by CUSG..
Coordinate with Office of Financial Aid to understand and address any issues related to the impacts of stipend-based compensation on student leaders.

Fiscal Management

Conduct high-level fiscal planning and reporting in partnership with the Finance Director, Finance Board Chair, CUSG Advisor, CUSG Office Manager, and Student Life Business & Finance, and CUSG.
Process purchase orders, standing purchase orders, and procurement for expenditure requests, ensuring compliance with university policies.
Place orders for office supplies, catering, event-related materials, and other operational needs.
Handle travel arrangements, reservations, and accommodations for CUSG members.
Ensure compliance with the Student Fee Regulations and all university policies.
Ensure all expenditures are appropriately authorized, documented, and reconciled.
Maintain organized financial records and expenditure files.

Finance Board and Joint Board Relations

Support the Finance Board Chair and CUSG Office Manager in managing the budget, financial tracking, and financial board processes.
Coordinate with Student Life Business & Finance to conduct regular check-in meetings and ensure compliance with university policies
Assist with processing invoices, tracking financial transactions, and entering data into financial systems.
Serve as a CUSG liaison between Joint Boards attending meetings and meeting with Chairs as necessary
Assist with Joint Board recruitment and onboarding as needed.
Assist in the design and facilitation of training and development for Joint Board Chairs and Members
Update records, ensuring transparency and accessibility for CUSG leadership and Joint Boards.
Help with website updates related to financial policies, budget allocations, and procurement procedures.

Duties as Assigned

What You Should Know

This is a hybrid work opportunity. The work schedule for this position is Monday - Friday 9:00AM - 5:00 PM, with flextime to attend Finance Board or Joint Board meetings that are later in the evenings.

What We Can Offer

The annual salary range for this full-time position is $58,200 - $65,000.
Onboarding assistance is available within the Student Life division guidelines.

Benefits

At the University of Colorado Boulder , we are committed to supporting the holistic health and well-being of our employees. Our comprehensive benefits package includes medical, dental, and retirement plans; generous paid time off; tuition assistance for you and your dependents; and an ECO Pass for local transit. As one of Boulder County’s largest employers, CU Boulder offers an inspiring academic community and access to world-class outdoor recreation. Explore additional perks and programs through the CU Advantage program.

Be Statements

Be courageous. Be visionary. Be Boulder.

What We Require

Bachelor’s degree in business administration, higher education, political science, finance, public administration, human resources, student affairs, or a related field; or equivalent combination of education and professional experience.
1 year of professional, administrative, student affairs, human resources, finance, payroll, operations, or related experience.
Experience working in a student-focused, collaborative environment that involves multiple campus partners.
Experience providing administrative support, coordinating projects, or managing operational processes.
Experience working with confidential or sensitive student information.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple contending priorities in a fast-paced environment.

What You Will Need

Experience working in higher education, student government, student affairs, shared governance, or advocacy-based workplaces.
Experience supervising, training, onboarding, or mentoring student employees.
Experience with payroll, timekeeping, student employment, or HR administrative processes.
Experience with budgeting, procurement, fiscal tracking, or financial reconciliation.
Experience coordinating hiring processes, interviews, and onboarding procedures.
Familiarity with CU Boulder software systems such as Handshake, Teams, Outlook, Concur,
PeopleSoft/HCM, or similar systems.
Experience supporting governing boards, committees, or legislative bodies.
Experience planning trainings, workshops, meetings, or leadership development opportunities.
Experience managing websites, databases, spreadsheets, or organizational records.
Demonstrated dedication to supporting student leadership, civic engagement, and inclusive organizational practices.

What We Would Like You To Have

Knowledge of administrative, operational, and organizational support practices.
Knowledge of human resources, payroll, budgeting, and procurement best practices.
Ability to interpret, explain, and apply university policies, procedures, and regulations.
Effective time management with outstanding attention to detail and accuracy.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to prioritize tasks, meet deadlines, and manage multiple projects simultaneously.
Ability to work independently while also collaborating effectively with diverse groups of students, staff, faculty, and campus partners.
Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment when handling sensitive information.
Ability to troubleshoot problems, identify solutions, and improve processes.
Ability to facilitate professional and positive interactions with students, staff, faculty, and campus partners.
Skill in using Microsoft Office Suite, Teams, Excel, Qualtrics, and virtual collaboration tools.
Ability to learn and adapt to new software systems and evolving university procedures.
Ability to support and engage students from a wide range of identities, backgrounds, and lived experiences.
Ability to supervise, train, and support student employees in a professional setting.

Special Instructions

To Apply, Please Submit The Following Materials

A current resume.
A cover letter that specifically tells us how your background and experience align with the requirements, qualifications, and responsibilities of the position.

We may request references at a later time.

Please apply by July 16, 2026
for consideration.

Environmental Project Scientist, Honolulu, Hawaii Posted:
06/19/2026

We are seeking a motivated Project Geologist, Project Scientist, or Project Engineer with a strong background in environmental remediation to join our Technical Services Organization. This mid-career role offers the opportunity to contribute to high-profile projects, develop technical leadership skills, and grow into a Technical Lead role on small to moderately complex assignments. This position must report to the CAPE office in Honolulu, Hawaii.

Responsibilities

Provide support for project planning, field sampling, quality control oversight, design evaluations, data analysis, and reporting.
Develop technical plans and reports including sampling and analysis plans, quality control plans, and construction completion reports.
Schedule and oversee field activities such as soil, surface water, and groundwater sampling, drilling, subcontractor management, and remediation system operation.
Support proposal development, cost estimating, and preparation of regulatory submittals.
Mentor junior staff and contribute to CAPE’s technical quality standards and procedures.
Collaborate with project and senior management to deliver high-quality results that meet budget, schedule, and client expectations.

Qualifications

Education: Bachelor’s degree in engineering, geology, or environmental science; advanced degree preferred.
Experience: Minimum 3 years in environmental remediation. Experience working in Hawaii/Tropical Pacific preferred.
Certifications/Training:
Preferred: Licensed Engineer or Geologist in Training (E.I.T. or G.I.T.) or able to obtain Professional Registration within six months of hire
HAZWOPER 40-hour training (and annual refresher).
Adult First Aid/CPR.
Valid U.S. driver’s license with satisfactory record.
U.S. citizenship required (due to federal contracting requirements).

Strong technical writing, analytical, and communication skills.
Familiarity with federal environmental regulatory programs (CERCLA, RCRA).
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and industry-standard tools (CAD, ArcGIS, modeling software).

Work Environment & Travel

Position requires up to 50% travel annually for project support.
Field conditions may involve exposure to varying weather, hazardous materials, and physical demands.

Salary

$80K - $102K commensurate with experience

WHY CAPE?

For 35 years, CAPE has delivered construction and environmental remediation solutions to governmental and private organizations nationwide. Our projects are high-profile environmental remediation projects involving cleanup of contaminated soil, groundwater, and sediment. The culture of our company is one of working together to achieve our clients’ objectives, company goals, and employees’

professional goals, and is succinctly and accurately defined as “We, Not Me” behavior. To ensure long-term, sustainable growth, we tailor our 3-year vision to be ahead of our industry in delivering our projects, align with our clients and team partners to improve our existing market share, and develop new services to support smart growth.

CAPE offers competitive benefits including Medical/Dental/Vision insurance, life insurance, ADP retirement savings plan including both traditional and Roth 401(k) with up to 4% match and lowest in class fees, health savings account (HSA) with investment option, flexible spending account (FSA), paid annual leave, paid maternity/paternity leave, and tuition reimbursement. CAPE also offers staff several other voluntary benefits options, as well as the option to work from home. Straight time overtime may be offered on certain field assignments.

CAPE is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. We invite all qualified applicants to apply to our open positions.

Maintain a current driver’s license in good standing and able to operate company owned vehicles.
Outdoor work in all weather conditions.
Willingness to work overtime when needed.
Familiarity and willingness to learn computer software (Auto CADD Civil 3D, Trimble Business Center)

Requirements:

0-3 years of experience as a Survey crew member or a new graduate with a technical degree in Surveying or Civil Design preferred but not required.
Ability to operate and maintain Trimble survey equipment including but not limited to robotic total stations, GPS survey equipment, data collection equipment, Automatic levels, preferred but not required.
Open and willing to perform some overnight-stay travel for work when needed.
Strong teamwork and communication skills.

Work in a team environment but also willing to work independently.

VillageCare: Our Story

VillageCare is a community-based, not-for-profit organization serving people with chronic care needs, as well as seniors and individuals in need of continuing care and managed care services. Our mission is to promote healing, better health and well-being to the fullest extent possible. Our care is offered through a comprehensive array of community and residential programs, as well as managed care. Make a difference as a Senior Financial Data Analyst - Healthcare

Your responsibilities will also include supporting the monthly close process, conducting claim reserve analysis, and creating member economics reports to aid strategic decision-making.

Additionally, you will lead medical claims reinsurance reporting, support the preparation of provider group financial statements, and ensure compliance with regulatory reporting requirements, all while demonstrating VillageCare's commitment to Service Excellence.

Additionally, the capacity to multi-task while maintaining a high level of attention to detail is vital for success in this role.

Strong communication skills, both verbal and written, along with robust presentation capabilities, will enhance collaboration with internal and external stakeholders. A Bachelor's degree in Healthcare, Finance, or a related field is required, or equivalent years of experience, to support your analytical and problem-solving abilities in a fast-paced setting.

Experience working in an actuarial function with a focus on building the claims reserve updating claims triangles and IBNR estimation 
Ability to perform complex data analysis and report/dashboard development in a health care setting

Position Summary:

We are seeking an organized, detail-driven BESS Project Coordinator to own the critical handoff between won proposals and live project execution. In this role, you ensure every won BESS engagement transitions into a fully documented, executable project plan — with complete scope, schedule, and resources — and you keep procurement moving by processing purchase orders, ordering materials and services to hit required on-site dates, and tracking orders from request through delivery. You are the connective tissue between Business Development, Operations, and Finance, driving on-time, well-organized project kickoffs and surfacing issues before they affect delivery. The ideal candidate is proactive, highly organized, and thrives coordinating many moving parts across teams.

Key Responsibilities:

Process purchase orders accurately and efficiently by reviewing internal communications and customer PO issuance.
Order materials and services on time, paying close attention to required on-site dates, and track orders from request through delivery.
Process purchase requests submitted via the company Purchase form and communicate all purchases to Accounts Receivable.
Monitor open orders and proactively resolve delivery delays, backorders, or discrepancies with vendors.
Own project setup: ensure all project files, contracts, specifications, and deliverables are organized, accurate, and accessible to execution teams.
Translate proposal commitments into actionable project scope, timelines, and resource requirements for seamless execution.
Schedule and facilitate internal and external project kickoff meetings with clear agendas, action items, and stakeholder alignment.
Maintain clear, proactive communication between Business Development, Operations, Engineering, and Finance to prevent gaps or delays.
Identify and escalate project setup issues or blockers early, ensuring they are resolved before impacting delivery timelines.
Maintain accurate project and procurement tracking logs, and provide status updates to stakeholders throughout the setup phase.

Required Qualifications:

2+ years of project coordination, procurement, operations, or administrative experience, ideally in construction, electrical, energy, or another project-based environment.
Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to track many concurrent projects and orders without dropping details.
Experience processing purchase orders and coordinating with vendors on materials, services, and delivery timelines.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills and comfort coordinating across internal teams and external stakeholders.
Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and Office, and the ability to learn project management and ERP / accounting systems.
Ability to anticipate problems, prioritize, and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

Preferred Qualifications:

Familiarity with Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), renewable energy, or utility-scale construction projects.
Experience supporting a proposal-to-execution or project-handoff process.
